rhetoricalPatterns.description: Sentence- and paragraph-level rhetorical shapes that mark AI-assisted prose, independent of any single buzzword.
rhetoricalPatterns.detection: detect-only: each match is a named pattern with a quoted line of evidence for a human to check; NOT folded into the numeric slop score
rhetoricalPatterns.attribution: Pattern set adapted from the 'No AI slop' editing skill by Peter Yang (github.com/petergyang/no-ai-slop, MIT); re-expressed as ontology detectors

BinaryContrast.label: Binary contrast
BinaryContrast.description: "It's not X. It's Y." / "not just X but Y" / "the question isn't X, it's Y." State Y directly.
BinaryContrast.example_slop: The question isn't the model. It's the eval.
BinaryContrast.example_fix: The eval matters more than the model.
BinaryContrast.keep_when: A genuine correction of a specific misconception, not a rhetorical flourish.

ColonReveal.label: Colon reveal
ColonReveal.description: A short capitalized phrase, a colon, then a lowercase dramatic reveal. Rewrite as a plain sentence.
ColonReveal.example_fix: It learns, which is the best part.
ColonReveal.keep_when: The colon introduces a list, label, quote, ratio, or code.

SuperficialAnalysis.label: Superficial analysis
SuperficialAnalysis.description: Trailing '-ing' clause that pretends to explain meaning (highlighting, underscoring, reflecting, showcasing).
SuperficialAnalysis.example_slop: The launch adds file search, highlighting the team's commitment to workflows.
SuperficialAnalysis.example_fix: The launch adds file search, so users find old drafts without leaving the editor.
SuperficialAnalysis.keep_when: The clause states a concrete consequence, not a vague virtue.

NegativeListingFragmentation.label: Negative listing & dramatic fragmentation
NegativeListingFragmentation.description: "Not a X. Not a Y. A Z." or "That's it. That's the whole thing." or stacked "X. And Y. And Z." Use complete sentences and say Z.
NegativeListingFragmentation.example_slop: Not a feature. Not a tool. A movement.
NegativeListingFragmentation.keep_when: Deliberate, sparing emphasis that fits the writer's spoken rhythm.

FakeStrongVerb.label: Fake-strong verb
FakeStrongVerb.description: "serves as / acts as / functions as a centralized hub/platform/solution." Prefer a plain verb, 'is', or 'has'.
FakeStrongVerb.example_slop: The app serves as a centralized hub for sponsor management.
FakeStrongVerb.example_fix: The app tracks sponsors, drafts, due dates, and approvals in one place.
FakeStrongVerb.keep_when: 'serves as' names a literal role and no plainer verb fits.

SynonymCycling.label: Synonym cycling
SynonymCycling.description: Rotating near-synonyms for one referent across adjacent sentences (the agent, then the assistant, then the tool). If the clear word is right, repeat it.
SynonymCycling.example_slop: The agent reviews the draft. The assistant scores it. The tool suggests fixes.
SynonymCycling.example_fix: The agent reviews the draft, scores it, and suggests fixes.
SynonymCycling.keep_when: The different words genuinely refer to different things.

HollowKickerRecap.label: Fake-profound kicker & summary-recap ending
HollowKickerRecap.description: A final 'deep' one-liner (aphorism/mic-drop) or a recap paragraph ('In conclusion', 'Ultimately', 'Overall'). End on the last concrete point, takeaway, or next action instead.
HollowKickerRecap.example_slop: In conclusion, AI is changing everything, and we must adapt.
HollowKickerRecap.example_fix: (end on the last concrete point already in the draft)
HollowKickerRecap.keep_when: A genuine call to action or concrete next step, not a restatement.
recap_openers: at the end of the day
when all is said and done

FormattingSlop.label: Formatting slop
FormattingSlop.description: Emoji in headings, bold sprinkled mid-sentence for emphasis, and em-dash clusters. Format should follow content, not decorate it.
FormattingSlop.keep_when: Emoji or bold is the platform's native style (e.g. a release changelog).

RoboticRhythm.label: Robotic rhythm
RoboticRhythm.description: Stacked punchy fragments and repeated sentence shapes — three or more very short sentences in a row. Vary shape only when it helps.
RoboticRhythm.example_slop: It works. It scales. It ships. Every time.
RoboticRhythm.example_fix: It works, scales, and ships every time.
RoboticRhythm.keep_when: A short burst used once, deliberately, for genuine emphasis.

limitations: Subjektivität binärer Slop-Urteile: Cohen's κ -0.15 bis 0.29 (Shaib et al. 2025) → dimensionale Bewertung robuster
Reflexivität: Detection-Heuristiken werden bekannt → Producer adaptieren ("humanized" Variants)
Falsch-Positive bei menschlichem Text: Templatierter Journalismus, Boilerplate
Kontextabhängigkeit: Technische Dokumentation darf Wiederholungen für Klarheit nutzen
Sprachliche Verzerrung: Detection auf Englisch am stärksten; geringer in Hindi, Vietnamesisch, Urdu — just dort wo viel Slop entsteht
Sich entwickelnde Modelle: Neue Modellgenerationen erzeugen neue Slop-Muster; Ontologie braucht regelmässige Updates
Philosophische Kritik (Puliafito): "Slop" beschreibt Mediokrität — aber Mediokrität ist Basislinie aller Kulturproduktion
